key_insight: The p-type a-Si:H emitter’s deep-trap density strongly controls recombination and band alignment at the heterojunction, and once it becomes too high the HIT cell performance collapses.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing emitter activation energy and limiting dangling-bond states are critical design levers for preserving Voc, fill factor, and high-efficiency HIT operation.
method: Simulated a-Si:H/c-Si HIT solar cells with an intrinsic layer in AFORS-HET.
Varied the deep-trap density of states in the p-type amorphous-Si:H emitter.
Tracked device metrics and electronic behavior across the heterointerface.
evidence_signal: The simulations show that beyond a critical deep-trap density, the built-in voltage drops, the depletion region shifts into the p-type a-Si, and the IV curve develops an S-shape with reduced Voc and fill factor.
watch_item: The reported gains depend on precise control of emitter defect density and activation energy, so real devices may be sensitive to fabrication variability and interface quality.
paper_title: Effect of deep-trap density of states for a-Si:H layers on HIT cell performances: Modeling Framework
